s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area
salient_findings: Discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla
Severe pruritus at the lesion sites
Lesions are well-circumscribed, violaceous, and annular without scale or erosion
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
3-month history of skin lesions
Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
Wood lamp examination was negative

shortlist.label: granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: matches pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions

shortlist.label: annular atrophic lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with localized, pruritic, annular lesions

shortlist.label: atopic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of pruritic, localized skin lesions

shortlist.label: eczema
shortlist.why_kept: may present with pruritic, violaceous lesions

shortlist.label: psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: can cause localized, pruritic, annular lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of violaceous, annular patches with severe pruritus, limited to the right axilla, along with biopsy findings showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, is most consistent with annular atrophic lichen planus.

rejected.label: granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions in a ring-like pattern, not violaceous patches

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: Usually involves multiple areas of the body and has a history of atopy, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: Similar to atopic dermatitis, eczema typically involves multiple areas and has a history of atopy

rejected.label: psoriasis
rejected.why: Characterized by scaly, erythematous plaques, which are not described in the patient's presentation
